newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River reopened near Memphis after fire.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River reopened near Memphis after fire.

text.p: The Mississippi River near Memphis, Tennessee, was reopened to shipping traffic early Friday, Coast Guard officials said.
A 20-mile stretch of the river used mainly by barges and tows was shut for 10 hours on Thursday after a chemical plant fire spewed toxic fumes into the air.
Eight vessels were held up during the closure between mileposts 650 and 670, but officials said there were no delays to maritime traffic this morning.
"As far as I know there are no vessels waiting," said Chief Warrant Officer Frank James with the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in Memphis.

Three firefighters were killed and 16 people were injured when an explosion tore through the BPS Inc. chemical plant in nearby West Helena, Arkansas, on Thursday. The blast released a poisonous cloud of chemicals and forced the evacuation of residents in neighboring communities.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
